title: Julio Herrera Velutini: Case Timeline, Bancrédito and Latest News
desc: Complete, sourced guide to banker Julio Herrera Velutini: the Wanda Vázquez case, Bancrédito’s FinCEN penalty, plea agreements, 2026 pardon, timeline, people and organisations involved.
summary: Venezuelan-born banker and owner of Puerto Rico–based Bancrédito. Indicted in 2022 with former Governor Wanda Vázquez and ex-FBI agent Mark Rossini; the case ended without trial through plea agreements in 2025 and, per Reuters, presidential pardons in January 2026.
status: Latest status: reported pardoned in January 2026. Allegations from the 2022 indictment were never tested at trial.
facts: U.S. v. Vázquez Garced et al., D. Puerto Rico
faq: Julio Martín Herrera Velutini is a Venezuelan-born banker who founded and owned Bancrédito International Bank & Trust Corporation in Puerto Rico. He was a co-defendant in the 2022 federal case involving former Governor Wanda Vázquez.

Prosecutors alleged in 2022 that Herrera Velutini and Mark Rossini promised campaign support to Vázquez in exchange for replacing the head of Puerto Rico’s financial regulator, which was investigating Bancrédito. The defendants denied wrongdoing.

There was no trial. In 2025 guilty pleas to a campaign finance violation were entered and the original charges were reported dismissed. In January 2026 Reuters reported that President Trump pardoned Herrera Velutini, Vázquez and Rossini.
What did FinCEN penalise Bancrédito for?
In September 2023 FinCEN assessed a $15 million penalty for Bank Secrecy Act violations: late suspicious activity reports, no due-diligence program for correspondent accounts, and no AML program.
No. The bank went into receivership and liquidation, which is why it is sometimes still described in present tense in filings.

people.name: Julio Herrera Velutini
people.desc: Venezuelan-born banker and owner of Bancrédito. Co-defendant in the 2022 federal case; pleaded not guilty in 2022. Reported to have been pardoned in January 2026.

people.name: Wanda Vázquez Garced
people.desc: Governor 2019–2021. Indicted in August 2022; pleaded guilty in August 2025 to a campaign finance violation; reported pardoned in January 2026.

people.name: Mark Rossini
people.desc: Former FBI agent who provided consulting services to Herrera Velutini. Third defendant in the 2022 indictment; reported pardoned in January 2026.

people.name: George Joyner Kelly
people.desc: Head of Puerto Rico’s financial regulator while it investigated Bancrédito. Prosecutors alleged efforts to remove him.

people.name: Víctor Rodríguez Bonilla
people.desc: Named OCIF commissioner in 2020; prosecutors alleged he had been recommended by Herrera Velutini.

people.name: Silvia Carreño-Coll
people.desc: Federal judge presiding over the criminal case in Puerto Rico.

events.name: Presidential pardons

timeline.title: Bancrédito founded
timeline.desc: Julio Herrera Velutini founds the Puerto Rico–based international banking entity.

timeline.title: Period of alleged BSA failures
timeline.desc: FinCEN later found the bank failed to file suspicious activity reports on time and lacked required AML controls.

timeline.title: Regulator change at OCIF
timeline.desc: Prosecutors allege Vázquez demanded the commissioner’s resignation and appointed a new one, a former consultant for Herrera Velutini’s bank.

timeline.title: Federal indictment
timeline.desc: Vázquez is arrested; Herrera Velutini (in England) and Rossini (in Spain) are charged. Herrera Velutini later pleads not guilty.

timeline.title: FinCEN penalty
timeline.desc: $15 million civil money penalty against Bancrédito. The parent company called it excessive and threatened legal action.

timeline.title: Plea agreements
timeline.desc: Vázquez pleads guilty to a campaign finance violation; the original bribery-related charges against Herrera Velutini are reported dismissed after a misdemeanor plea.

timeline.title: Presidential pardons
timeline.desc: The Justice Department’s clemency list shows pardons for Vázquez, Herrera Velutini and Rossini; a White House official called the case “political prosecution.” Opposition figures condemned the move.

summary: Puerto Rico international banking entity founded in 2008. Fined $15 million by FinCEN in September 2023 for Bank Secrecy Act violations and later wound down in receivership and liquidation.
status: Latest status: in liquidation; $15M FinCEN penalty (2023) — its parent company disputed the action.
faq: Bancrédito International Bank & Trust Corporation was a Puerto Rico international banking entity founded in 2008 by Julio Herrera Velutini and serving foreign banks in Central America and the Caribbean.
FinCEN assessed a $15 million civil penalty on September 15, 2023 for willful Bank Secrecy Act violations between October 2015 and May 2022.
Yes. The bank is in a prolonged receivership and liquidation process under regulatory supervision.
How is Bancrédito linked to the Wanda Vázquez case?
Prosecutors alleged the bribery scheme aimed to remove the regulator investigating Bancrédito. The case ended in pleas and pardons rather than a trial.
